title: scheduled-llm-gate-inspection
intention: Scheduled probes fire LLM prompts to Hex for periodic inspection of gate feedback. The sieve stays deterministic Python; what changes is what it is calibrated against. The LLM reviews accumulated feedback and proposes parameter adjustments.
why: A sieve that measures at 100% match rate cannot show efficacy — it agrees with everything. The feedback the sieve collects is where efficacy hides, but nobody reads it. Hex reviewing the feedback on a schedule closes the loop: the sieve measures, the feedback accumulates, the LLM reads the feedback, the parameters adjust, the sieve measures differently.
traces_to: Law 4 — a gate whose parameters never adjust from evidence is policy wearing physics' clothes. The adjustment loop is what makes it physics.
learns-its-gates founding intention — the system learns its gates from evidence; a hand-set constant in a gate is a learned value stranded in a human's head.
sieves-measure-not-judge — the sieve stays deterministic Python; the LLM reviews feedback PERIODICALLY, never in the measurement path.
Law 1 — Hex reading accumulated feedback is compiling the observation once; a human re-reading the same feedback each session is re-deriving.

falsifier.proves_green: THREE things must work: (1) a gate collects feedback in a shape Hex can read — structured JSON, not prose, carrying the sieve's input, its output, and the gate owner's disposition if any; (2) a scheduled probe fires an LLM prompt to Hex with the accumulated feedback and receives a proposed parameter adjustment; (3) the adjustment lands THROUGH the gate's own door (Law 6 — the gate owner approves or rejects). The gate owner is the component, not the LLM — Hex proposes, the gate's physics accepts or refuses.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the LLM is in the measurement path — a sieve that calls an LLM to DECIDE is not deterministic and violates sieves-measure-not-judge; (2) the adjustment bypasses the gate owner's approval — the gate's own door is the only write path (Law 6); (3) the schedule is a polling loop or a daemon rather than a probe fired by an event that already fires (shrinking-footprint: event not poll); (4) the feedback shape is not parseable by a local LLM — Hex is the M1 Studio box, not CC, and the feedback must be structured enough for a smaller model to read; (5) a parameter adjustment that makes the sieve WORSE has no rollback path — the adjustment must be reversible by the same door it entered through.
falsifier.horizon: After the feedback tool's route is built (cairn/tools/feedback) and at least one gate collects structured feedback. There is no point adjusting parameters nobody collects yet. The feedback tool is upstream; this ticket is the CONSUMER of what it produces.

how: Build scheduled probes that fire LLM prompts to Hex for periodic gate inspection. The sieve stays deterministic Python; the LLM adjusts parameters periodically. The probe fires on a schedule, not on every gate crossing.

chart_notes.orient: The feedback accumulates beside the gate that produces it, in structured JSON. The prompt to Hex carries the accumulated records and the current parameter values. inference_domain is the sole path to Hex.
chart_notes.constrain: OUT: the LLM in the measurement path (the sieve stays deterministic Python); a new daemon or timer (the probe fires from an existing event); CC as the reviewer (Hex is cheaper and local). IN: the adjustment loop, the feedback shape, the gate owner's approval door.
chart_notes.validate: A parameter adjustment proposed by Hex and accepted by the gate owner changes the sieve's output on the same input. The before/after is measurable: same input, different disposition, and the feedback that motivated the change is named in the adjustment record.
